findings.claim: Solanio and Salerio taunt him about Jessica’s elopement (repeated in the Key Fact and on a flashcard).
findings.truth: Act 3 Scene 1 opens 'Enter Solanio and Salarino'; the two who taunt Shylock and hear 'Hath not a Jew eyes?' are Solanio and Salarino. Salerio is a separate character who arrives from Venice in Act 3 Scene 2 and appears at the trial.

findings.claim: “I will have my bond. I will not hear thee speak.” (also a memorisation flashcard)
findings.truth: The line is 'I’ll have my bond. I will not hear thee speak.' (Act 3 Scene 3). 'I will have my bond' is a real line elsewhere in the same speech, but not in this sentence.

findings.claim: It was first published as a comedy, and it does end with marriages and restored fortunes.
findings.truth: The 1600 first quarto did not call it a comedy (Stationers' Register, 22 July 1598: 'the Marchaunt of Venyce or otherwise called the Jewe of Venyce'). The play was first grouped with the comedies in the 1623 First Folio.
findings.evidence: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Merchant_of_Venice — 'classified as a comedy in the First Folio'; Stationers' Register entry 22 July 1598

findings.truth: Jessica has four speeches in that exchange, so she is not silent there. Her real silence is the rest of Act 5: her last line in the play is 'I am never merry when I hear sweet music', after which she says nothing for roughly 250 lines. The sentence now points at that.

findings.truth: 'Hath not a Jew eyes?' is itself in prose, not verse. As written the lesson invites students to claim a prose-to-verse ascent that the text does not support — a direct AO2 error. Both places now say the speech is prose whose rhetoric matches verse for force.

findings.claim: All 48 practice questions across the 8 lessons are labelled '[20]' with type '20 marks — Extract Analysis' / '20 marks — Wider Text Response' and a 'Top band (17–20)' ladder.
findings.truth: The spec gives the Shakespeare section 40 marks in total and never states a per-question split, so every '20' here is unverifiable from the spec. Two options: (a) relabel the whole family to marks-free labels ('Extract question' / 'Whole-play essay') and rescale every band ladder, which is ~96 field writes across this unit alone and should be one consistent decision for every Eduqas Shakespeare unit; or (b) leave the labels and fix them in the queued question-type relabel pass. Recommendation: (b) — hold for the fleet-wide relabel, since a unit-local change would leave the other five Eduqas Shakespeare texts inconsistent.

summary: 25 findings over 8 lessons, 29 edits. The dominant fault is the exam frame: five lessons label context as AO4 or name the board (or its spec code) in student-facing text, when the Shakespeare section assesses AO1, AO2 and AO4 (accurate writing) and credits no context objective. Text errors: Salerio for Salarino in Act 3 Scene 1, a misquoted 'I'll have my bond', 'All that glisters' attributed to Portia, a Much Ado character inside a Merchant sentence, 'Hath not a Jew eyes?' implied to be verse, Jessica called silent in a scene where she speaks, and the play said to be first published as a comedy. No lesson is finding-free, but lesson 2's only finding is a NOTE and lesson 4's are LOW.
